required_outcomes: Treats the tenant's email at event 024 as written consent for the provider to collect the office keys and enter on Monday 20th PM while the tenants are away, and records that consent in the case.
Confirms the Monday 20th PM visit to the provider with key-collection arrangements (collect from the office, lock up, return the keys afterwards) and sets the visit in the case record.
Replies to the tenant confirming the arrangement and that the keys will be returned to the office after the visit.
Sets a follow-up after the visit to check the work result and that the keys are back.
acceptable_alternatives: Letting the landlord know the visit is going ahead with office keys while the tenants are away, as long as the visit is still confirmed to the provider.
Asking the tenant for a contact number while abroad in the same confirmation message, without making the visit conditional on it.
Querying with the provider that 20 October 2024 is a Sunday, not a Monday, before fixing the date, provided the tenant's key consent is recorded and the tenant is not asked to re-confirm it.
positive_behaviours: Tells the provider there will be no pets in the flat on the day, as the tenant said.
Asks the provider to report back with photos or a note of the work, since nobody will be home to confirm it.
red_flags: Refusing or delaying entry, or insisting on someone being home or on serving 24 hours' notice, when the tenant has already given written consent.
Escalating the key arrangement to a human, or asking the tenant to re-confirm consent they have just given in writing.
prohibited_actions: Moving the visit until after the tenants return on 5 November despite their consent, leaving the plumbing fault unrepaired for three more weeks.
critical_failures: Ending the turn without confirming the keyed visit to the provider (or asking the provider to settle the day), so the job stalls despite the tenant's written consent.
